links.comparator_used: Pre-implementation period, before the interruptive BPA alert was deployed (observational before/after); also alert fired vs not fired
links.outcome: Drug-induced QT prolongation (diLQTS) risk after deployment of the interruptive alert-based CDS
links.effect: diLQTS after CDS deployment vs before: OR 1.13 (95% CI 0.94-1.36; P=.21). Provider response to the alert had no effect on diLQTS (P=.79). Inpatient mortality after deployment: OR 1.43 (95% CI 1.09-1.88).
links.tradeoff: Only 60.13% of alerts were complied with within the BPA, and 32.19% of alerts were followed by the culprit medication being ordered anyway. Hospital stay was longer when the alert fired (IRR 1.08). Mortality was higher after deployment, though the authors suspect unmeasured confounding rather than a causal effect of the CDS.
links.quote: After adjustment for age, sex, race and ethnicity, location, laboratory findings, medication, and comorbidity clusters, there was no difference in risk of diLQTS based on CDS deployment (OR 1.13, 95% CI 0.94-1.36; P =.21; Table S10A in Multimedia Appendix 1 ), and no evidence of effect for any individual medication ( P =.98; Table S10B in Multimedia Appendix 1 ).

design_hint: alert-based CDS deployment with pre/post outcome evaluation and analysis of provider alert responses
